corrections.text: The article presents three quotations as verbatim source text that are actually paraphrases. It quotes 9to5Mac as saying Apple's new Pencils are "launching alongside iPad Pro devices in spring 2027"; 9to5Mac's actual text is "set for launch next year alongside new iPad Pro models in spring 2027." It quotes 9to5Mac as saying iPhones "may already comply through Apple's Self Service Repair program"; 9to5Mac's actual text is "Apple may be in compliance already due to the availability of the Self Service Repair program." It quotes Engadget as saying Apple "switched to USB-C on the iPhone 15 lineup due to similar regulatory pressure"; Engadget's actual text is "the momentous shift to USB-C with the iPhone 15 lineup," with no matching verbatim phrase. The underlying facts in all three cases are accurate; only the quoted wording was not verbatim.

The article states that "Both 9to5Mac and AppleInsider describe the current Apple Pencil in identical terms: 'a hunk of plastic filled with glue' that is 'virtually impossible to repair.'" This phrasing is AppleInsider's alone ("the Apple Pencil is a hunk of plastic filled with glue and is virtually impossible to repair"). 9to5Mac does not use this language; it describes the Pencil as held together with "lots of internal adhesive." The fact that the Pencil is difficult to repair is accurate for both outlets, but the quoted phrase should not have been attributed to 9to5Mac.
